Thanks @madhusudan1997sharma and @llew2011 for the heap dumps! Looking into the latest one.

- Opened the heapdump with YourKit, I can find the KeyedWeakReference class.
- Wrote a test that runs the LeakCanary heap dump analysis code on that heap dump on a JVM and calls HeapAnalyzer#findTrackedReferences. Got a crash, same issue: `snapshot.findClass(KeyedWeakReference.class.getName())` returns null.

* The Snapshot has absolutely 0 classes available.
* Turns out, parsing the Hprof is failing silently, perflib throws an exception while parsing the heap dump, catches it, logs it and then keeps going as if nothing happened.

```
java.lang.NullPointerException
	at com.squareup.haha.perflib.HprofParser.loadNativeStack(HprofParser.java:445)
	at com.squareup.haha.perflib.HprofParser.loadHeapDump(HprofParser.java:327)
	at com.squareup.haha.perflib.HprofParser.parse(HprofParser.java:186)
	at com.squareup.leakcanary.HeapAnalyzerHeapDumpTest.foo(HeapAnalyzerHeapDumpTest.java:46)
```

In this specific example, we're trying to read a native stack. We parse the thread serial number, get 2, and then ask the current heap for the thread object. The current heap only has one thread with serial number 1 (added earlier), so it returns null => NPE

I set up a non suspending breakpoint in Heap.addThread that triggers on `serialNumber == 1` and evaluates `mThreads.put(2, thread)`. That worked around the crash (for the purpose of this test), and I got a proper leak trace:

```
* Toast$TN.!(mNextView)!
* ↳ LinearLayout.!(mContext)!
* ↳ ServicerOrderActivity
```

So really it looks like there's something about this heap dump, it's got a thread (serial number = 2) that we never find, yet we get its stacktrace to parse and cannot.

I tried listing all the GC Roots of type RootType.NATIVE_STACK in that heap dump. 

There are 3 GCRoots pointing to the main thread (serial 1), 708 GC roots pointing to this unknown thread (serial 2), and then the rest is all the threads that are already visible in YourKit.

Sounds like there might be something wrong with how Android dumps the heap and it's missing some of the thread information? YourKit just ignores it, and perflib crashes.

Stepping through with a debugger, we get a ThreadObject, a native stacks, a bunch of jni locals and then java frames for thread 1. Then we immediately get a native stack for thread 2, no thread object.

Extra note: we get those 708 "native stack" objects and absolutely nothing else related to thread 2, then we get the thread object for thread 3. So no extra information to figure out what this is about.

I tried updating HAHA to latest perflib and still had the issue. Then I tried loading those heap dumps in Android Studio and they looked empty (they're not, as YourKit shows).

I've filed a bug to perflib: https://issuetracker.google.com/issues/122713143
We'll have to wait for perflib to fix this, then wait for the next source publish. Then we'll update perflib (#1133) and then this should go away.

issue.title: Update to HAHA 2.1

repository.name: leakcanary
repository.description: A memory leak detection library for Android.

issue.body:
* Removed "computeIgnoredBitmapRetainedSize": we added this hack because some bitmaps were not added to the total retained sized because they had a native gc root dominator. This only worked pre M because we looked at mBuffer which went away. The updated perflib looks up in native land and updates the Bitmap objects to the correct native size. This change means we now get the exact same retained size in Android Studio & LeakCanary. Unless we build our own heap dump parser, it's probably better to just rely on perflib for retained size. 
* HAHA now ignores missing native threads instead of creating an empty snapshot.
* HAHA 2.1 has Java 8 bytecode, which means LeakCanary consumers are now expected to support Java 8 bytecode. This is a breaking change that will go in a 2.0 release.

Fixes #1133 (update to latest perflib)
Fixes #1124 (crash)
